steps.heading: Finding the gaps
steps.body: Missing data shows up as NaN. isna() marks every missing cell as True (notna() is the inverse), so it can drive a boolean filter just like any other condition.

steps.heading: Which rows are incomplete?
steps.caption: You can't compare to NaN with == — it never matches, even against itself. isna() is the only reliable check.

steps.heading: Drop it, or fill it
steps.body: dropna() removes rows with gaps (how='any' by default — any missing column disqualifies the row). fillna() keeps every row and replaces the gaps with a value: a constant, the column mean, or the nearest known neighbor (ffill/bfill).

steps.heading: A sensible default instead of losing the row
steps.output: # missing revenue replaced by the average of the known values
steps.caption: You'll practice dropna() variants (subset, how, thresh) and fillna() variants (scalar, mean, ffill/bfill) in the cards that follow.
